content:
Hi all! I've been building a Lean 4 game theory library on top of Mathlib and wanted to gauge interest in upstreaming parts of it.
The library currently covers:

  • Normal-form games - pure/mixed Nash equilibrium, Nash existence via Brouwer fixed point, dominance (strict/weak), correlated equilibrium
  • Extensive-form games - game trees with chance/decision nodes, behavioral strategies, subgame-perfect equilibrium, Kuhn's theorem (behavioral iff  mixed equivalence under perfect recall)
  • Key theorems - Zermelo's backward induction theorem, one-shot deviation principle, von Neumann minimax theorem, potential games and the finite improvement property
  • Multi-agent influence diagrams (MAIDs) - DAG-based representation with a verified reduction to extensive-form games
    Everything is built on discrete probability (PMF) with a unifying KernelGame abstraction (stochastic kernel from joint strategies to outcomes) that solution concepts are defined on once, with concrete representations bridging to it.
    For the existence of mixed Nash equilibrium, I'm using a Brouwer fixed-point theorem from a separate GitHub repo (not yet in Mathlib), so that proof currently depends on an external package.
    The repo is at https://github.com/elazarg/GameTheory (Mathlib v4.27.0, ~3100 build targets, builds clean).
    Would any of this be a good fit for Mathlib? I'm happy to start with whatever slice would be most useful - maybe basic normal-form games and Nash equilibrium, or the probability kernel infrastructure. Any feedback on design choices is also welcome.

Ruben Van de Velde said:

cc Violeta Hernández

Wrong kind of game theory! This is game theory in the economist's sense, rather than the combinatorialist's.

There is some prior work in #13248. There were plans to start a separate repo for this, perhaps even one within the leanprover organization, but it seems nothing ever came of this. Quoting from that thread:

The main issue with this PR is that none of the current Mathlib maintainers is an expert in this area.

Unless the situation has somehow changed (which I doubt), I'd recommend to keep your work within your own repository.
Oops. All I know is that neither is the kind of game I'd play in my free time :)
Most probably this would be much better as a downstream library.

Violeta Hernández said:

There is some prior work in #13248. There were plans to start a separate repo for this, perhaps even one within the leanprover organization, but it seems nothing ever came of this. Quoting from that thread:

https://github.com/math-xmum/gametheory came out of it I think

I think getting strategic interactions game theory into mathlib would probably require an extensive discussion on what the right definition of a normal form game is. It would probably have to be extremely general, like most of mathlib. For example, if you imagine trying to formalize an infinitely-repeated Cournot duopoly game, at each stage your game consists of an infinitely large strategy space, and then when you mix strategies you can no longer describe them with PMFs. So getting this into mathlib would require being very careful about how this interacts with topology.

Because of this, I would say that the easiest things to get into mathlib are anything that can be set up without referencing game theory, e.g. the Kakutani fixed point theorem or the minimax theorem.
